prompt:
Larder now serves two kitchens. Add sites as schema 3:
- Every location belongs to a site (`site` on each location) and the data has a `sites` list. Existing locations belong to site `main`. Add a second site `annex` ("Annex kitchen") with one location `annex-fridge` ("Annex fridge", 4 °C) to data/seed.json.
- A request names its site in the `X-Larder-Site` header; without it the site is `main`. An unknown site is a 400 error with its own error code.
- Batches, stock on hand, cooking, alerts, the stock value report and stock-takes only see the request's site. Items, suppliers, recipes and dishes are shared.
Older data files must still open. Update the tests that assume the old schema.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Sites are added as schema 3. Older files still open: the new v2→v3 migration adds a `sites` list containing `main` ("Main kitchen") and puts every existing location in `main`. The seed now also has the `annex` site with the `annex-fridge` location. Requests pick their site with the `X-Larder-Site` header (default `main`). An unknown site is a 400 with the new code `unknown_site`. Batches, stock on hand (including stock.csv), cooking, alerts, the stock value report and stock-takes only see the request's site; a batch belongs to the site of its location. Items, suppliers, recipes and dishes are shared. `npm test` (34 pass) and `npm run lint` pass, and a schema 2 file migrates with `larder migrate`. Gaps I left alone: (1) temperature limits are looked up by location id (`fridge`, `freezer`), so `annex-fridge` gets no 5 °C limit and no daily-check alert. (2) The nightly job, forecasts, waste report and ledger export still count all sites. (3) Receiving an order does not check that the location is in the request's site. (4) Unrelated to this change: batches are used newest-received first instead of first-expired-first (FEFO), against docs/DATA.md.
